meta.title: ymzz-notion — Your daily review, already waiting
meta.desc: Free, open-source automation: every morning GitHub Actions creates your Notion daily review, emails you the link, and syncs yesterday to Google Sheets and Git.
hero.eyebrow: Open source · by 晏銘湛箴
hero.identity: ymzz-notion is a free, open-source GitHub template that prepares your daily journal in Notion every morning and keeps a copy of yesterday in Google Sheets and Git.
intro.p1: A small automation you copy into your own GitHub account. Once set up, it runs by itself every day — there is no app to open and no server to pay for.
intro.p2: At the time you choose, it creates today's blank review page in your Notion, sends you one email with the link, and copies yesterday's entry into a Google Sheet and a Markdown file in your repository.
intro.who.p: Anyone who wants a daily review habit: makers, students, investors keeping a trading journal, teams running KPT retros.
intro.own.p: Only in your own Notion, your own Google account and your own repository. Nothing passes through a server of ours.
intro.cost.p: Nothing. It uses GitHub's free Actions minutes and the free Notion and Google APIs. No AI quota.
before.a1: You mean to journal, but the blank page is never ready.
before.a2: Notes scatter across apps; last month is lost.
before.a3: Holdings live in a broker app with no reasoning attached.
before.b1: Today's page is waiting, with a link in your inbox.
before.b2: Every day lands in a Sheet you can chart and in Git forever.
before.b3: Each position has a thesis, a stop and a daily snapshot.
f1.p: Score, mood, energy, Keep / Problem / Try, decisions, top 3 for tomorrow, deep-work hours.
f2.p: Ticker, platform, cost, value, weight, thesis, stop/target — snapshotted daily so you see how it changed. Works for IBKR or any broker (entered by you).
f3.p: One email linking to the page created in step ①, at the hour you choose, in your own time zone.
f4.p: Yesterday lands in Google Sheets for charts and as Markdown in your repo — a permanent, diffable archive.
f5.p: UTC 07:00 by default. Set two repo Variables and it is yours; filenames carry your zone.
f6.p: Add Obsidian, Telegram, CSV… by dropping in one file.

s0.p: Wakes every hour and exits in seconds unless it is your time and today hasn't run.

s2.p: Links straight to the page from ①.

sink.p: Every destination is a sink with the same three fields. Missing settings? It skips itself.
setup.sub: About 15 minutes, once. Progress is saved only in this browser.
t1.b:
1. Open the GitHub repo and choose Use this template → Create a new repository (or Fork).
  2. Make it Private — your reviews are stored there.

Public repos get unlimited Actions minutes; a private repo uses roughly 720 min/month (24 short runs a day), within GitHub Free's 2,000.
t1.x: No “Use this template” button? Use Fork instead.
t2.b:
1. Open Notion → Integrations → New integration (Internal), name it ymzz, copy the token.
  2. Open the Notion page that should hold your reviews → ⋯ → Connections → add ymzz.
t2.x: setup.sh says “object not found”? The page isn't connected to the integration yet.
t3.b: On your computer (Node.js 20+), create the two blank databases:
t3.x: On Windows use the PowerShell lines below.
t4.b:
1. Google Cloud Console → new project → enable Google Sheets API.
  2. IAM → Service accounts → Create → Keys → Add key → JSON.
  3. Create a Google Sheet and share it with the service-account email as Editor. The part in /d/SHEET_ID/edit is your SHEET_ID.
t4.x: “The caller does not have permission”? The Sheet isn't shared with the service account.
t5.b:
1. Turn on 2-Step Verification for your Google account.
  2. Create one at App passwords — you get a 16-character password.
t5.x: Page not available? 2-Step Verification is off, or a work account blocks it.
t6.b: Repo → Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions → New repository secret. Add each name:
t6.x: Secrets stay in your GitHub. Never paste them into a website, including this one.
t7.b: Default is UTC 07:00. Pick yours — for example America/Los_Angeles (Pacific) — and copy the generated settings.
t7.x: GitHub schedules can run a few minutes late; the gate catches up on the next hour.
t8.b:
1. Actions → daily-review → Run workflow.
  2. Success: an email arrives, today's page appears in Notion, and your Sheet gets two tabs.
  3. From now on it runs by itself.
t8.x: A red run? Open it — the failing step names the missing secret. You also get a failure email.
tz.vars: Option A — GitHub → Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions → Variables:
tz.utc: First hourly gate after your time (UTC)
a1: Yes. It runs on GitHub's free Actions minutes and free Notion/Google APIs. There is no paid tier.
a2: In your Notion, your Google account and your repository. This website stores only your language, theme and setup progress in your browser (localStorage). No cookies, no trackers.
a3: You get an email with a link to the failed run. The next hour retries automatically, because a day is only marked done after success.
a4: GitHub pauses schedules after 60 days without commits. Each run re-enables the workflow and adds a keepalive commit after 45 quiet days.
a5: Yes — every field is defined in one file, scripts/schema.mjs.
